question: Which among the following covalent compounds will have the least number of shared electron pairs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**H₂**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Covalent compounds** are formed when atoms share electrons to achieve a full outer shell and attain stability. Each shared pair of electrons forms a covalent bond. 
 
• **O₂** (Oxygen molecule): Consists of a double bond between two oxygen atoms, which means it involves two shared pairs of electrons (4 electrons in total). 
 
• **N₂** (Nitrogen molecule): Consists of a triple bond between two nitrogen atoms, meaning it involves three shared pairs of electrons (6 electrons in total). 
 
• **CH₄** (Methane): Each hydrogen atom shares one electron with the carbon atom, forming four single covalent bonds. Therefore, methane has 4 shared electron pairs. 
 
• **H₂** (Hydrogen molecule): Consists of a single covalent bond between two hydrogen atoms, involving only one shared pair of electrons (2 electrons in total). This is the **least number of shared electron pairs**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Covalent Bonding:** 
 
 
• Occurs between non-metallic elements where atoms share electrons to achieve a stable electronic configuration (similar to a noble gas). 
 
• Examples include molecules like H₂, O₂, N₂, and CH₄. 
 
• Depending on the number of shared electron pairs, covalent bonds can be classified as single, double, or triple bonds. 
 
 
 
• **Types of Covalent Bonds:** 
 
 
• **Single Bond:** Involves one shared pair of electrons (e.g., H₂, Cl₂). 
 
• **Double Bond:** Involves two shared pairs of electrons (e.g., O₂, CO₂). 
 
• **Triple Bond:** Involves three shared pairs of electrons (e.g., N₂, C₂H₂). 
 
 
 
• **Electron Pair Sharing:** 
 
 
• Each shared electron pair corresponds to a covalent bond. 
 
• In molecules with multiple bonds (double or triple), more electron pairs are shared compared to single bonds. 
 
 
 
• **Stability of Covalent Compounds:** 
 
 
• The stability of a covalent compound depends on the strength of its bonds. Triple bonds (e.g., in N₂) are stronger than double or single bonds. 
 
• Hydrogen (H₂), having a single bond, is less complex in terms of shared electron pairs. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **H₂:** The simplest molecule, involving only one shared pair of electrons, making it the molecule with the least number of shared electron pairs in the given options. 
 
• **Bond Order:** The number of shared pairs of electrons correlates directly with the bond order (e.g., single bond = bond order 1, double bond = bond order 2). 
 
• **Applications:** Hydrogen (H₂) is widely used in industries (e.g., ammonia production, hydrogen fuel cells) due to its simple molecular structure and chemical properties.
